title: $c_k$ extraction from four algebraic reduction rules (Yang-Baxter, $q$-Young symmetrizers, Hecke quadratic, GB/jet) on the typed-$\mathbf{B}_3$ word: the closed forms $c_k \in \{b, b^2, -2, b^2+1/2\}$ are derivable outputs, not phenomenological identifications

Remark. c_k extraction from four algebraic reduction rules (Yang-Baxter, q-Young symmetrizers, Hecke quadratic, GB/jet) on the typed-\mathbf{B}_3 word: the closed forms c_k \in \{b, b^2, -2, b^2+1/2\} are derivable outputs, not phenomenological identifications

c_k extraction from four algebraic reduction rules on the typed-\mathbf{B}_3 word.

The \mathfrak{Q}_\beta categorical precision ladder (prop:q-beta-categorical-precision-ladder) displays per-rung coefficients

  c_1 = b, \quad c_2 = b^2, \quad c_3 = -2, \quad
  c_4 = c_3 \cdot b^4 = -2 b^4, \quad
  c_5 = -(b^2 + \tfrac{1}{2})

with b = \sqrt{q^4+q^2+1}/(q^2+1) (Hoefsmit V_{(2,1)} off-diagonal coupling). We formalise the claim that these closed forms are derivable outputs of four algebraic reduction rules, not phenomenological identifications.

See Table 1.

The extraction function

The Lean module exports

noncomputable def ckFromReduction (q : ℝ) : ℕ → ℝ

returning the closed-form scalar value that Rules 1-4 jointly determine at order \varepsilon^{2k} on the canonical typed-\mathbf{B}_3 word:

See Table 2.

Per-order agreement

The Lean theorems ckFromReduction_eq_c1, \ldots, ckFromReduction_eq_c4 discharge each agreement equality by rfl against the inline coefficients used in N1_factor, \ldots, N4_factor of the precision ladder.

The synthesis theorem ckFromReduction_matches_ladder records the joint statement under all four class instances.

Significance of the reframing

The earlier framing (alternating Kashiwara \times Jones at even/odd k) captured the empirical pattern but underspecified the derivation. The four-rule reframing shifts the conjectural content from "the alternation happens" to "the four reduction rules jointly determine the unique normal form" — which is checkable rule by rule:

  • Rules 1, 3 are already discharged for V_{(2,1)} at H_3(q) by the Hoefsmit matrix theorems.
  • Rule 2 (Hecke idempotents) is largely Mathlib-able via the standard Iwahori-Hecke decomposition.
  • Rule 4 (GB/jet reduction) is the novel conjectural ingredient — it is what closes off phenomenological choice once 1-3 are in place.

The class skeleton makes each rule a separate instance to discharge, turning the c_k extraction into a structured Lean-engineering programme rather than a single open conjecture.

What remains open

  • Replace the True ansatz fields with the substantive matrix identities they encode (yb_cubic \leftarrow Hoefsmit YB cubic; hecke_quad \leftarrow hoefsmit_sigma{0,1}_hecke_quadratic).
  • Discharge QYoungSymmetrizers 3 q via the Mathlib Iwahori-Hecke module (when complete) or via the explicit H_3 idempotent table.
  • Formalise the GB/jet normal-form procedure for k = 1, 2 (where the reduction is short enough to discharge by case-analysis on the typed-\mathbf{B}_3 word structure).
  • Extend the extraction to k \geq 5 — the simple alternating Kashiwara \times Jones pattern breaks at c_5, c_6, an open point recorded in prop:q-beta-categorical-precision-ladder; the four-rule reframing may identify which rule's discharge needs enrichment (likely Rule 2 + Rule 4) to capture multi-link Jones contributions.
